fullPassage:
(A)
My two girls grew up without challenges with respect to development and social interaction. My son Benjamin, however, was quite delayed. He struggled through his childhood, not fitting in with the other children and wondering what he was doing wrong at every turn. He was teased by the other children and frowned upon by a number of unsympathetic adults. But his Grade 1 teacher was a wonderful, caring person who took the time to ask why Benjamin behaved the way he did.

(B)
I suspected the teacher had paid for it out of his own pocket. It was a story-board book with a place for a photo. On each page there was an outline of an animal and a hole so that the face in the photo appeared to be the face of the animal. Wondering if Benjamin would really be interested in the book, I brought it home. He loved it! Through that book, he saw that he could be anything he wanted to be: a cat, an octopus, a dinosaur — even a frog!

(C)
The teacher was determined to understand Benjamin and to accept him as he was. One day he came home with a note from his teacher. He suggested I go to the school library. They were having a sale, and he thought my son would like one of the books. I couldn't go for a couple of days and was concerned I'd missed the opportunity. When I finally went to the school, his teacher had set aside the book for my little boy.

(D)
Benjamin joyfully embarked on an imaginative journey through the book, and it laid the foundation for his future success. And thankfully, his teacher had taken the time to observe and understand him and find a way to help him step outside his own world and join ours through a story-board book. My son later became a child actor and performed with a casting company in Toronto for seven years. He is now a published author writing fantasy and science fiction! Who would have guessed?
